ai-at-work.title: Startup Battlefield 200 applications close today: Nominate a founder or submit your startup

ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch's Startup Battlefield 200 competition is closing applications today, offering one hundred thousand dollars in equity-free funding and a stage to pitch in front of investors. For digital workplace professionals building tools that solve real collaboration or productivity problems, this is one of the few legitimate funding opportunities where you won't get drowned out by AI hype. If you've got something that actually works and solves a pain point your customers face every day, it's worth the twenty minutes to throw your hat in the ring before midnight.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch is pushing early bird ticket sales for their 2026 Disrupt conference, offering savings of up to $410 before prices jump on May 29th. For digital workplace leaders, these conferences can expose you to emerging collaboration tools and workplace tech trends worth evaluating. That said, most of what gets announced at Disrupt won't meaningfully impact your actual workplace for 18 months, so maybe sleep on it and catch the session recordings instead of rushing to spend $1500+ on a ticket.

ai-at-work.title: SOND, a sleep tech startup from Bose’s former head of sleep, exits stealth with $7M
ai-at-work.excerpt: SOND, a startup led by Bose’s former head of sleep products, emerged from stealth with $7M in funding for its AI-powered sleep earbuds.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: A sleep tech startup called SOND just raised $7 million to sell AI-powered earbuds designed to improve how people sleep. This matters because employee wellness programs are becoming table stakes for attracting talent, and sleep quality directly impacts productivity and mental health at work. That said, I'll believe the ROI story when I see it, because most wellness gadgets end up gathering dust in desk drawers next to those standing desk converters nobody actually uses.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic launches Cowork, a Claude Desktop agent that works in your files — no coding required
ai-at-work.excerpt: Anthropic released Cowork on Monday, a new AI agent capability that extends the power of its wildly successful Claude Code tool to non-technical users — and according to company insiders, the team bui
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic just released Cowork, an AI agent that lets regular people automate file work in Claude Desktop without writing code, and they built the whole thing in ten days using their own AI tool. This matters because it's the first time a mainstream AI company has delivered something genuinely useful to non-technical workers instead of just hyping "agents coming soon." If it actually works as advertised, your users might finally have a reason to care about AI beyond chatting with a very smart paperclip.

tools-tech.title: How I got my business emails through spam filters with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC
tools-tech.excerpt: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are three DNS-based authentication records that stop your emails from landing in spam and prevent criminals from spoofing your domain.
tools-tech.dwp_take: A guy figured out how to properly configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records so his business emails actually reach people instead of rotting in spam folders. This matters because nothing kills collaboration faster than when your carefully crafted messages vanish into the void, and poor email authentication is still one of the most preventable problems in most organizations. Here's the thing: if you're not already running these three protocols, you're essentially hoping your emails make it through on good vibes and prayers, which is a strategy that has never worked in the history of email.

tools-tech.title: I found an easy way to automatically keep AI out of my search results - and it works in nearly every browser
tools-tech.excerpt: You can add a custom search engine in your browser that excludes all AI results. I'll show you how to do it in every major browser.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Someone figured out how to filter AI-generated garbage out of search results by creating custom search engine parameters that exclude AI content from major search engines. This matters because your employees are already drowning in AI slop cluttering their research, and IT leaders need to know there are actual workarounds beyond just hoping Google cleans up its own mess. The fact that we've reached the point where blocking AI results is now a basic productivity tool tells you everything you need to know about where we are right now.

tools-tech.title: Why the future of AI is on-premises - business advice from Dell Tech World 2026
tools-tech.excerpt: With rising costs, sovereignty requirements, and agent adoption, Dell's latest conference focused on how enterprises can transition AI workloads to a hybrid infrastructure.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Dell's telling enterprises that the future of AI isn't living in someone else's cloud, it's coming home to roost on your own servers. Digital workplace leaders need to hear this because it directly impacts infrastructure spending, security decisions, and whether your company controls its own data or keeps renting compute from hyperscalers. Here's the thing though: "on-premises is the future" is exactly what server vendors say when cloud costs spike, so take it with a grain of salt while also taking seriously the sovereignty and cost arguments that actually hold water.

tools-tech.title: Apple’s iPhone satellite ambition goes beyond rescuing hikers
tools-tech.excerpt: Apple has spent billions of dollars to develop satellite connectivity for iPhone; I very much doubt it did so solely to rescue stranded hikers. The company will most certainly have had a bigger prize
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple is building out satellite connectivity for iPhones to create an alternative network infrastructure beyond traditional cellular coverage. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because it signals how consumer device capabilities are reshaping expectations around always-on connectivity and redundancy in enterprise environments. Here's the thing though: most organizations will spend the next five years figuring out how to secure and manage satellite connections while their users are already using them.

digital-culture.title: How to know if your solo business needs to evolve, innovate, or pivot
digital-culture.excerpt: Ever get the feeling that you need to make a change in your business? Your pipeline has dried up, your prospective clients’ needs have changed, or something just feels “off”? Companies have entire tea
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece talks about how solo business owners need to recognize when it's time to evolve, innovate, or pivot their operations. This matters to digital workplace folks because remote work and distributed teams mean more of your colleagues are running independent practices or consulting gigs on the side, and they're often struggling with strategic planning in isolation. Here's the thing: solopreneurs aren't some separate species from your corporate workforce anymore, and if your organization doesn't understand what independent workers actually deal with, you're missing insights about flexibility, autonomy, and what your best people might be thinking about.

digital-culture.title: How AI inhibits our curiosity, and what to do to regain it, according to science
digital-culture.excerpt: Curiosity is one of the most consequential forces in human history. Every scientific breakthrough, technological leap, and cultural advance begins not with knowledge, but the desire to know. At its co
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new study suggests that AI tools are actually suppressing human curiosity by giving us answers before we've had a chance to wonder about the questions. This matters to digital workplace professionals because we're now managing teams where knowledge workers can get instant answers instead of doing the critical thinking that builds expertise and innovation. Here's the thing: if your workplace strategy is just plugging AI into everything without thinking about what you're losing, you've already lost the plot.

digital-culture.title: Sam Altman is ‘delighted to be wrong’ about AI destroying jobs
digital-culture.excerpt: Unlike some of his industry peers, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has been surprisingly skeptical of the notion that AI is displacing workers. In an interview a few months ago, he argued that AI is a convenien
digital-culture.dwp_take: Sam Altman is walking back the "AI will eliminate all jobs" narrative, saying companies are using AI as cover for layoffs they'd planned anyway. This matters because your executives are probably using the same AI excuse when you know the real story involves cost-cutting and poor planning. It's refreshing to see someone in tech admit uncertainty, though I'd feel better about it if we weren't all just watching companies use AI as the convenient villain while they downsize.

digital-culture.title: Technology x humanity: A conversation with Dayforce’s Amy Capellanti-Wolf
digital-culture.excerpt: The HR leader shares her take on the rise of AI, hybrid work and retaining talent.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Dayforce's Amy Capellanti-Wolf sat down to discuss how AI, hybrid work, and talent retention are reshaping HR technology. Digital workplace pros need to pay attention because this is where the actual business impact happens—it's not about the tools, it's about whether your people stick around and do their best work. The real test isn't whether your company has AI; it's whether you've figured out how to use it without making your employees feel like they're working alongside a calculator.

industry-news.title: Google AI Studio Cheat Sheet: Features, Pricing, and More
industry-news.excerpt: Google AI Studio lets users test Gemini models, build apps, generate media, and export code. Here’s what it does, costs, and where it falls short. The post Google AI Studio Cheat Sheet: Features, Pric
industry-news.dwp_take: Google released AI Studio, a tool that lets people experiment with Gemini models, build applications, create media, and pull out working code without touching the command line. This matters because your knowledge workers are already playing with these tools whether IT approves or not, so you need to understand what they're actually doing and where the security and governance gaps live. The real question isn't whether AI Studio is good or bad, it's whether your organization has a plan for when your staff starts building internal tools with it and then forgets to tell you.

industry-news.title: The Next AI Security Failure May Start With a Trusted Assistant
industry-news.excerpt: AI coding tool flaws highlight the need for data-layer governance, access controls, encryption, and audit logs for AI agents. The post The Next AI Security Failure May Start With a Trusted Assistant a
industry-news.dwp_take: TechRepublic is warning that AI coding assistants have security gaps that could let bad actors slip through via trusted tools we're already using. This matters because most organizations are throwing these tools at their workforce without governance frameworks, meaning your developers might be leaking credentials or proprietary code without even realizing it. Here's the thing: we've built a trust relationship with AI assistants that we haven't actually earned yet, and we're bolting it straight into our infrastructure like it's going to behave itself.

industry-news.title: SK Hynix Tops $1 Trillion Valuation as AI Memory Boom Reshapes Chip Market
industry-news.excerpt: SK Hynix crossed a $1 trillion valuation as AI data center demand drives memory chip prices higher and reshapes the semiconductor market. The post SK Hynix Tops $1 Trillion Valuation as AI Memory Boom
industry-news.dwp_take: SK Hynix just hit a trillion dollar valuation thanks to AI-driven demand for memory chips that's reshaping the entire semiconductor market. This matters to you because your organization's infrastructure costs are about to get real interesting when you're competing for the same memory and compute resources that everyone else suddenly needs for their AI projects. Here's the thing: your CFO is going to start asking hard questions about why your digital workplace platform upgrades are getting more expensive, and the honest answer is that the entire tech supply chain just got a lot pricier.

industry-news.title: Meta Layoffs Leave Employees Wary Despite Zuckerberg’s Reassurance
industry-news.excerpt: Meta employees are questioning Mark Zuckerberg’s pledge to avoid more company-wide layoffs this year as the company restructures around AI. The post Meta Layoffs Leave Employees Wary Despite Zuckerber
industry-news.dwp_take: Meta employees are skeptical about leadership's promise of no more layoffs after recent cuts and ongoing AI-driven restructuring. This matters because it shows how quickly employee trust erodes when companies make strategic pivots without clear communication about what that means for individual jobs. The real lesson here isn't about Meta specifically, it's that telling people "no more layoffs" while simultaneously restructuring departments is like saying "we're definitely keeping this sandwich together" while actively reorganizing the fillings.
